key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving photoluminescence and preserving electronic uniformity, even under accelerated aging.
engineering_relevance: Surface smoothness alone may be an unreliable quality metric when designing durable perovskite solar cells.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Combine statistical AFM topography analysis with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare capped and pristine films for emission and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting than pristine films.
watch_item: The abstract reports film-level results without quantitative effect sizes or device-level efficiency and operational-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
